Write \(K_A(w)=K(A\mid w)\) and \(F_K^f(w)=\sum_{A\in\mathcal A}f(A)K_A(w)\). Then \(0\le F_K^f\le R_f\), and Fubini's theorem gives
\[
 E_hF_{K_s}^f(W)
 =\int F_K^f(x)\,dN_d\{h,(1+s^2)\Sigma\}(x).
\]
The unsmoothed expectation is the same integral with \(N_d(h,\Sigma)\). For \(P_s=N_d\{h,(1+s^2)\Sigma\}\) and \(P_0=N_d(h,\Sigma)\), direct substitution in the Gaussian likelihood ratio gives
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(P_s\Vert P_0)
 =\frac d2\{s^2-\log(1+s^2)\}.
\]
For \(x\ge0\), \(x-\log(1+x)\le x^2/2\), because the derivative of \(x^2/2-x+\log(1+x)\) is \(x^2/(1+x)\). Hence
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(P_s\Vert P_0)\le \frac{ds^4}{4}.
\]
Let \(A\) be a likelihood-ratio upper level set attaining total variation and put \(v=P_s(A)-P_0(A)\ge0\). The log-sum inequality reduces relative entropy to the binary experiment on \(\{A,A^c\}\). For binary probabilities \(q+v\) and \(q\), two differentiations in \(v\), followed by minimization over \(0\le q\le1-v\), give
\[
 \operatorname{KL}\{\operatorname{Bern}(q+v)\Vert\operatorname{Bern}(q)\}\ge2v^2.
\]
Thus the elementary Pinsker bound yields
\[
 \|P_s-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le \sqrt{\operatorname{KL}(P_s\Vert P_0)/2}
 \le s^2\sqrt{d/8}.
\]
The total-variation distance is also at most one. Since the difference of the expectations of a function with range in \([0,R_f]\) is at most \(R_f\|P_s-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\), this proves
\[
 \sup_h\left|E_hf\{K_s(W)\}-E_hf\{K(W)\}\right|
 \le R_f\min\{1,s^2\sqrt{d/8}\}.
\]
For the pointwise modulus, \(K_s(w)\) is obtained by applying the Markov kernel \(K\) to \(N_d(w,s^2\Sigma)\). Contraction of total variation under a Markov kernel therefore gives
\[
 \|K_s(w)-K_s(w')\|_1
 \le 2\|N_d(w,s^2\Sigma)-N_d(w',s^2\Sigma)\|_{\mathrm{TV}}.
\]
If \(a=\|w-w'\|_{\Sigma^{-1}}/s\), the likelihood-ratio halfspace calculation for two equal-covariance Gaussian laws gives their total-variation distance as \(2\Phi(a/2)-1\). Since \(\Phi(x)-1/2\le x/\sqrt{2\pi}\) for \(x\ge0\),
\[
 \|K_s(w)-K_s(w')\|_1
 \le \sqrt{\frac2\pi}\,\frac{\|w-w'\|_{\Sigma^{-1}}}{s}.
\]
All divisions use \(s>0\), and the Mahalanobis norm is defined because \(\Sigma\succ0\).

Choose the tangential coordinates so that the columns of \(B_\sigma\) are orthonormal after whitening by \(\Sigma^{-1/2}\), and let \(U_T\) be uniform on \([-T,T]^k\), where \(T>0\). The displayed average is
\[
 Q_T(w)=E\{K_s(w+t u+B_\sigma U_T)\}.
\]
For \(a\in\mathbb R^k\), contraction under the kernel \(z\mapsto K_s(w+t u+B_\sigma z)\) implies
\[
 \|Q_T(w+B_\sigma a)-Q_T(w)\|_1
 \le \|\mathcal L(U_T+a)-\mathcal L(U_T)\|_1.
\]
In one coordinate the last \(L^1\)-distance is \(\min\{2,|a_i|/T\}\). Coupling the product uniforms coordinate by coordinate, or equivalently bounding the symmetric difference of the two boxes, gives
\[
 \|\mathcal L(U_T+a)-\mathcal L(U_T)\|_1
 \le \min\left\{2,\frac{\|a\|_1}{T}\right\}.
\]
This proves the first assertion without any limiting behavior of \(K\).

For the second assertion, the \(\Sigma\)-orthogonal quotient decomposition makes the residual tangential observation \(B_\sigma Z\), with \(Z\sim N_k(0,I_k)\), independent of the normal coordinate and parameter-free. If \(p,p'\) are two action distributions and \(0\le f\le R_f\), the zero-sum identity for \(p-p'\) gives
\[
 \left|\sum_A f(A)\{p_A-p'_A\}\right|
 \le \frac{R_f}{2}\|p-p'\|_1.
\]
Conditioning on the normal coordinate and using the first bound with \(a=Z\),
\[
 \left|E f\{Q_T(W_N+B_\sigma Z)\}-E f\{Q_T(W_N)\}\right|
 \le \frac{R_f}{2T}E\|Z\|_1
 =\frac{R_fk}{T\sqrt{2\pi}},
\]
because \(E|Z_i|=\sqrt{2/\pi}\). The bounded-normal-chart condition is used only to ensure that the declared quotient chart and the associated coverage or separated-risk mean set are valid throughout this averaging operation.

Put \(F_i^f(w)=\sum_A f(A)q_{i,A}(w)\) and \(F_{\widetilde K}^f(w)=\sum_i\lambda_i(w)F_i^f(w)\). Orient every path from the anchor \(a(C)\) to \(i\). Telescoping along that path gives
\[
 F_i^f(w)-F_{a(C)}^f(w)
 =\sum_{e\in\pi_C(i)}\{F_{e^+}^f(w)-F_{e^-}^f(w)\}.
\]
Multiplication by \(\lambda_i(w)\ge0\), summation over \(i\), and the triangle inequality imply
\[
 |F_{\widetilde K}^f(w)-F_{a(C)}^f(w)|
 \le \sum_e g_{C,e}(w)|F_{e^+}^f(w)-F_{e^-}^f(w)|,
 \qquad
 g_{C,e}(w)=\sum_{i:e\in\pi_C(i)}\lambda_i(w).
\]
Both endpoint functionals lie in \([0,R_f]\). Splitting the integral for edge \(e\) over \(P_{C,e}\) and \(P_{C,e}^c\) consequently yields, for every \(h\in M_{C,f}\),
\[
 \begin{split}
 E_h\!\left[g_{C,e}(W)|F_{e^+}^f(W)-F_{e^-}^f(W)|\right]
 &\le \int_{P_{C,e}}g_{C,e}|F_{e^+}^f-F_{e^-}^f|\phi_\Sigma(w-h)\,dw\\
 &\quad+R_f\int_{P_{C,e}^c}g_{C,e}\phi_\Sigma(w-h)\,dw\\
 &\le \Gamma_{C,e}^f.
 \end{split}
\]
Thus the left side in the claim is at most \(\sum_e\Gamma_{C,e}^f\). The supremum is over the entire declared mean set and therefore includes seam-centered means.

For completeness, let \(d_i=\lambda_i(W)-\lambda_i(h)\). Since \(\sum_i d_i=0\) and \(0\le F_i^f\le R_f\),
\[
 \left|\sum_i d_iF_i^f(W)\right|
 \le \frac{R_f}{2}\sum_i|d_i|.
\]
Taking \(E_h\) proves the separate weight-variation estimate \(R_f\omega(h)/2\). Adding this nonnegative certified remainder to the sharper path bound proves the stated inequality.

Let \(m=|\mathcal A|\), let \(\mu\) be Lebesgue measure on \(\mathbb R^d\), and represent a rule by \(p=(p_A)_{A\in\mathcal A}\), where \(p_A\in L^\infty(\mu)\), \(p_A\ge0\), and \(\sum_Ap_A=1\) almost everywhere. Denote this set by \(\mathscr K\). It is convex. We verify the compactness needed below directly. On each box \(B_j=[-j,j]^d\), every coordinate of every sequence in \(\mathscr K\) has \(L^2(B_j)\)-norm at most \(\mu(B_j)^{1/2}\). Choose a countable orthonormal basis of \(L^2(B_j)\), diagonally extract convergence of all Fourier coefficients, and use Bessel's inequality to obtain a weak \(L^2(B_j)\) limit. A second diagonal extraction over the finitely many actions and the boxes gives consistent measurable limits \(p_A\). Testing against the negative part of \(p_A\), the positive part of \(p_A-1\), and \(\sum_Ap_A-1\), all of which lie in \(L^2(B_j)\), proves \(0\le p_A\le1\) and \(\sum_Ap_A=1\) on every box. Thus \(p\in\mathscr K\). The coefficient metric makes this sequential compactness into compactness on \(\mathscr K\).

For \(h\in D_v\) and \(g\in H_r\), define
\[
 c_{v,h}(p)=\int\phi_\Sigma(w-h)\sum_{A\ni v}p_A(w)\,dw,
 \qquad
 r_g(p)=\int\phi_\Sigma(w-g)\sum_A\ell(A)p_A(w)\,dw.
\]
On each box a Gaussian density is in \(L^2\), so local weak convergence gives convergence of its integral; outside an increasing box the error is bounded by its Gaussian tail because \(0\le p_A\le1\). Hence every \(c_{v,h}\) and \(r_g\) is continuous on \(\mathscr K\). Therefore
\[
 \mathscr K_\eta=\bigcap_{v\in V}\bigcap_{h\in D_v}
 \{p:c_{v,h}(p)\ge1-\eta\}
\]
is compact. It is nonempty because the rule which always reports \(V\) belongs to it. The function \(p\mapsto\sup_{g\in H_r}r_g(p)\) is a supremum of continuous functions and is lower semicontinuous. It attains its minimum on \(\mathscr K_\eta\), proving primal attainment. Since every Gaussian shift is equivalent to Lebesgue measure, changing the \(L^\infty\) representative on one common null set gives an actual measurable Markov kernel for every mean.

Let
\[
 \alpha_v=\sum_{j=1}^{J_v}a_{vj}\delta_{h_{vj}},\quad
 a_{vj}\ge0,\ h_{vj}\in D_v,
 \qquad
 \beta=\sum_{i=1}^I b_i\delta_{g_i},\quad
 b_i\ge0,\ \sum_i b_i=1,\ g_i\in H_r.
\]
Write
\[
 a_v(w)=\int\phi_\Sigma(w-h)\,\alpha_v(dh),
 \qquad
 b(w)=\int\phi_\Sigma(w-g)\,\beta(dg).
\]
The Lagrangian infimum over \(\mathscr K\) is pointwise and equals
\[
 \mathcal D(\alpha,\beta)
 =(1-\eta)\sum_v\alpha_v(D_v)
 +\int\min_{A\subseteq V}
 \left\{b(w)\ell(A)-\sum_{v\in A}a_v(w)\right\}\,dw. \tag{1}
\]
Indeed, the integrand is a finite linear function of the action simplex, whose minimum is achieved at a vertex. For every honest \(p\),
\[
 \mathcal D(\alpha,\beta)
 \le \sum_i b_i r_{g_i}(p)
 +\sum_{v,j}a_{vj}\{(1-\eta)-c_{v,h_{vj}}(p)\}
 \le \sup_{g\in H_r}r_g(p).
\]
Taking the infimum over honest \(p\) proves that every finite atomic dual is a valid lower certificate.

For the converse, fix \(t<M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\). The open sets
\[
 \{p:r_g(p)>t\},\quad g\in H_r,
 \qquad
 \{p:c_{v,h}(p)<1-\eta\},\quad h\in D_v,
\]
cover \(\mathscr K\): an honest \(p\) has risk strictly larger than \(t\), and a nonhonest \(p\) violates at least one coverage constraint. Compactness gives a finite subcover, with risk points \(g_1,\ldots,g_I\) and coverage points \((v_j,h_j)\), \(j=1,\ldots,J\). Consequently no \(p\in\mathscr K\) makes all coordinates of
\[
 y(p)=\bigl((r_{g_i}(p)-t)_{i\le I},
 ((1-\eta)-c_{v_j,h_j}(p))_{j\le J}\bigr)
\]
nonpositive. The compact convex set \(y(\mathscr K)\) and the closed negative orthant are disjoint. Taking their nearest points and expanding the squared-distance inequality supplies nonnegative coefficients \(\gamma_i,\zeta_j\), not all zero, and a number \(q>0\) such that
\[
 \sum_i\gamma_i\{r_{g_i}(p)-t\}
 +\sum_j\zeta_j\{(1-\eta)-c_{v_j,h_j}(p)\}\ge q
 \quad\text{for every }p\in\mathscr K. \tag{2}
\]
The full-set rule has every coverage deficit equal to \(-\eta\). Thus \(\sum_i\gamma_i>0\); otherwise (2) fails for that rule. Normalize by \(G=\sum_i\gamma_i\), set \(b_i=\gamma_i/G\), and set \(a_j=\zeta_j/G\). Then (2) says that the corresponding finite-atomic Lagrangian has infimum strictly larger than \(t\). By (1), \(\mathcal D(\alpha,\beta)>t\). Since \(t<M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\) was arbitrary, soundness and separation prove
\[
 M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)=\sup_{\alpha,\beta\ {\rm finite\ atomic}}\mathcal D(\alpha,\beta).
\]

Finally, every \(D_v\) is a finite union of rational polyhedra. The set \(H_r\) is semialgebraic over the rational input: membership is expressed using the finitely many rational inequalities for the \(D_v\)'s and the quadratic Mahalanobis-distance inequality, with closest-point variables eliminated by enumerating active sets. Rational isolating boxes enumerate a dense family of real-algebraic points in every positive-dimensional piece and the exact algebraic point in every zero-dimensional piece. Gaussian translation is continuous in \(L^1\), so moving finitely many support points within this family and approximating their weights by rationals changes (1) arbitrarily little. Dovetail all finite rational encodings and retain the running maximum of certified dual values. This sequence is nondecreasing and converges to the displayed supremum, without bounding spatial support.

Fix \(p\). First let \(P\in\mathcal F(p)\). Because \(X\), both treatment responses, both selection responses, and both wage responses have finite support, the realized vector
\[
 R=\{D^{\mathrm{pot}}(0),D^{\mathrm{pot}}(1),S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0),S^{\mathrm{pot}}(1),Y^{\mathrm{pot}}(0),Y^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)\}
\]
takes values in a finite set. No defiers puts its treatment coordinates in the declared monotone set. Conditional weak selection monotonicity puts every positive-mass complier type in \(\mathcal R_x\). Define \(\lambda_{xr}=P(X=x,R=r)\). Then \(\lambda\ge0\) and \(\sum_{x,r}\lambda_{xr}=1\).

Conditional randomization and the known assignment probabilities give
\[
 \begin{split}
 P(X=x,Z=z,D=d,S=s,Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=y)
 &=\bar\pi_z(x)\sum_{r\in\mathcal R_x}\lambda_{xr}
 \mathbf 1\{D_r(z)=d,S_r(d)=s,\\
 &\hspace{40mm}y=Y_r(d)\text{ if }s=1,\ 
 y=\dagger\text{ if }s=0\}\\
 &=(T_0\lambda)_{x,z,d,s,y}.
 \end{split}
\]
The three consistency assumptions justify these substitutions. Hence \(T_0\lambda=p\). Instrument--stratum positivity gives \(\sum_r\lambda_{xr}=P(X=x)\ge\pi_*\).

Dividing observed cells by \(\pi_z(x)>0\), then using randomization and consistency, shows
\[
 c_{axk}(p)=P\{X=x,D^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)>D^{\mathrm{pot}}(0),
 S^{\mathrm{pot}}(a)=1,Y^{\mathrm{pot}}(a)=y_k\}. \tag{3}
\]
For \(a=1\), subtraction cancels always-takers; for \(a=0\), the factor \(2a-1=-1\) reverses the subtraction and cancels never-takers. Summing (3) gives \(q_{ax}=P(X=x,\text{complier},S^{\mathrm{pot}}(a)=1)\). Binary directional selection monotonicity then gives
\[
 m_x=\min(q_{0x},q_{1x})
 =P\{X=x,\text{complier},S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)=S^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)=1\}.
\]
Thus the final constraint in \(\Xi(p)\) is precisely aggregate target positivity, and \(\lambda\in\Xi(p)\).

Conversely, let \(\lambda\in\Xi(p)\). Draw \((X,R)\) with masses \(\lambda_{xr}\); conditional on \(X=x\), draw \(Z\) independently of \(R\) from \(\bar\pi_z(x)\); and set observed variables by the consistency maps. The support \(\mathcal R_x\) gives no defiers and complier-conditional selection monotonicity. The construction gives randomization and all consistency and exclusion restrictions. The inequalities in \(\Xi(p)\) give stratum and target positivity. Finally \(T_0\lambda=p\), so the law is in \(\mathcal F(p)\). The two constructions prove exact equivalence and the nonemptiness consequence.

By fiber--polytope equivalence, \(\Xi(p)\) is nonempty. It is a closed subset of a finite-dimensional probability simplex and hence compact. For \(\lambda\in\Xi(p)\), let
\[
 H_a^\lambda(j)=\sum_{x,r}\lambda_{xr}
 \mathbf 1\{r\text{ is an always-selected complier},\ Y_r(a)\le y_j\},
 \qquad
 M^\lambda=\sum_{x,r}\lambda_{xr}\mathbf 1\{r\text{ is an always-selected complier}\}.
\]
The fiber constraint gives \(M^\lambda\ge m_*>0\). On the finite ordered grid,
\[
 Q_{a,P_\lambda}(t)=y_j
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 H_a^\lambda(j)\ge tM^\lambda
 \ \text{and}\ 
 [j=1\ \text{or}\ H_a^\lambda(j-1)<tM^\lambda]. \tag{4}
\]
All quantities are linear in \(\lambda\). For a fixed pair \((j_0,j_1)\), the common-slack program replaces each strict predecessor inequality by \(H_a^\lambda(j_a-1)\le tM^\lambda-\gamma\) and maximizes \(\gamma\). Its optimum is positive exactly when one \(\lambda\in\Xi(p)\) realizes both quantiles in (4). Every \(\lambda\) realizes one of finitely many pairs, and every feasible pair is realized by its selected basic maximizer.

The effect takes values in the finite set \(\{y_{j_1}-y_{j_0}:1\le j_0,j_1\le J\}\). Choosing the feasible pair with smallest difference therefore equals the infimum over \(\Xi(p)\), and the selected maximizer induces one \(P_t^-(p)\in\mathcal F(p)\). Applying (4) to that same law in both arms gives
\[
 Q_{1,P_t^-(p)}(t)-Q_{0,P_t^-(p)}(t)=\underline\Delta(t;p).
\]

The compactness and quantile characterization (4) in the lower-endpoint proof apply unchanged. The positive common-slack program for \((j_0,j_1)\) is feasible exactly when one \(\lambda\in\Xi(p)\) realizes both grid quantiles. Selecting the feasible pair with largest \(y_{j_1}-y_{j_0}\), and then its lexicographically least positive-slack basic maximizer, produces one \(P_t^+(p)\in\mathcal F(p)\) satisfying
\[
 Q_{1,P_t^+(p)}(t)-Q_{0,P_t^+(p)}(t)
 =\max_{\lambda\in\Xi(p)}
 \{Q_{1,P_\lambda}(t)-Q_{0,P_\lambda}(t)\}
 =\overline\Delta(t;p).
\]
The maximum exists because this objective has finite range on the nonempty compact fiber.

Fix an experiment in \(\mathfrak E_K\). The covariance is positive definite, \(K_{\mathrm{par}}\) is compact, the label regions cover it, and \(H_r^K\ne\varnothing\). Let \(K\in\mathcal C_\eta^K\) have risk at most \(M_K(r)+a\), where \(a>0\). Gaussian smoothing at scale \(s>0\) gives coverage at least \(1-\eta-t_s\) and risk at most \(M_K(r)+a+Dt_s\), where \(t_s=\min\{1,s^2\sqrt{d/8}\}\).

Compactness gives \(R<\infty\) such that
\[
 \sup_{h\in K_{\mathrm{par}}}P_h\{W\notin[-R,R]^d\}\le q.
\]
Replace the rule outside this box by \(V\); coverage cannot decrease and risk rises by at most \(Dq\). On the box, use a rational observation mesh of Mahalanobis diameter \(b\) and rational simplex rounding with \(L^1\)-error \(\zeta\). The smoothing modulus bounds every \([0,R_f]\)-valued expectation error by
\[
 R_f\left\{\frac12\sqrt{\frac2\pi}\frac b s+\zeta\right\}.
\]
Thus the finite rational rule has a computable coverage deficit \(\rho\to0\) and risk at most \(M_K(r)+a+o(1)\). Mixing with \(V\) with probability \(\rho/(\eta+\rho)\) restores exact honesty and adds at most \(D\rho/(\eta+\rho)\). Sending \(a,s,q,b,\zeta\) to zero proves density.

For lower bounds, repeat the finite-subcover and finite-dimensional separation proof of atomic duality with means restricted to \(D_v^K\) and \(H_r^K\). Every number below \(M_K(r)\) is exceeded by a finite-prior Lagrange dual. Hence finite-prior values converge upward and repaired gridded-primal values converge downward.

Gaussian probabilities of rational boxes are computable by truncating the exponential series with an explicit remainder. Suprema over the compact rational polytope are enclosed by a rational mean mesh and the Gaussian-shift modulus. Enumerate mesh, rounding, integration, and finite-prior precisions, retain outward endpoints, and stop at the first gap below the requested rational accuracy. Convergence proves termination. No recession object is used.

Put \(q=49/25\) and whiten \(w=(a,b)\) to \(z=(a/\sqrt{1/8},b/\sqrt{3/20})\). Every row of every \(F_v\) has Euclidean norm one. If \(h\in D_v\), both inward facet means are nonnegative. The union bound gives
\[
 P_h\{v\notin Q_q(W)\}\le2\Phi(-q).
\]
The alternating exponential series, integrated on rational intervals and combined with \(0.3989422804014<(2\pi)^{-1/2}<0.3989422804015\), gives
\[
 0.0249978951482<\Phi(-49/25)<0.0249978951483.
\]
Thus \(2\Phi(-49/25)<0.0499957902966<0.05\), proving global honesty, including equality faces.

Let \(h\in H_2\) have unique label \(v\). Separation by two implies that both standardized inward facet means are at least two. If both observed inward coordinates exceed \(q\), all rivals are excluded, so the loss is zero. The two standardized facet noises have correlation at least \(\rho_*=-\sqrt{3/13}\). With \(t=2-q=1/25\), monotonicity of the Gaussian orthant probability in its correlation gives
\[
 P_h\{Q_q(W)=\{v\}\}\ge\Phi_2(t,t;\rho_*).
\]
Direct differentiation gives
\[
 \frac d{du}\Phi_2(u,u;\rho_*)
 =2\phi(u)\Phi\!\left(u\sqrt{\frac{1-\rho_*}{1+\rho_*}}\right)
 \ge\phi(u),\qquad u\ge0.
\]
The centered polar integral is
\[
 \Phi_2(0,0;\rho_*)=\frac14-\frac{\arctan\sqrt{3/10}}{2\pi}.
\]
Therefore
\[
 \sup_{h\in H_2}E_h\ell\{Q_q(W)\}
 \le \frac34+\frac{\arctan\sqrt{3/10}}{2\pi}
 -\{\Phi(1/25)-1/2\}. \tag{5}
\]
Outward series arithmetic gives
\[
 0.0797514300099<\frac{\arctan\sqrt{3/10}}{2\pi}<0.0797514300101,
 \qquad
 0.0159534368527<\Phi(1/25)-\frac12<0.0159534368530.
\]
The right side of (5) is below \(0.8137979931574<0.813799\).

For the lower certificate, let \(\mu_\pm=(\pm1/\sqrt2,2)\) and \(\mu_0=(0,2)\). The Mahalanobis distance of \(\mu_+\) from the rival across \(a=0\) is two and all other rival distances exceed two; symmetry treats \(\mu_-\). Thus both risk atoms lie in \(H_2\). In the standardized first coordinate \(z\), the risk-mixture density divided by \(\phi(z)\) is \(e^{-2}\cosh(2z)\). For
\[
 a_0=1028/625,\qquad \lambda_0=e^{-2}\cosh(2a_0),
\]
the curves cross at \(z=\pm a_0\). Pointwise minimization over actions reduces the dual integral to the minimum of the risk-mixture density and \(\lambda_0\phi(z)\), so
\[
 D_0=\Phi(a_0-2)-\Phi(-a_0-2)
 +\lambda_0\{2\Phi(-a_0)-1/10\}. \tag{6}
\]
Outward rational series bounds give
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 1.8181887545408<\lambda_0<1.8181887545411,\\
 0.3612198823625<\Phi(a_0-2)<0.3612198823627,\\
 0.0001337999106<\Phi(-a_0-2)<0.0001337999108,\\
 0.0500055310938<\Phi(-a_0)<0.0500055310941.
 \end{gathered}
\]
Hence \(D_0>0.3611061955936\). Replacing \(\lambda_0\) by \(\lambda_4\) changes (6), including its penalty, by less than \(3753/10^{15}\). Thus \(L_4>0.3611061955898>0.361100\). Atomic-dual soundness gives the lower endpoint.

At \(r=0\), honesty at the common contact \(h=0\) gives
\[
 E_0|K(W)|=\sum_{v\in V_4}P_0\{v\in K(W)\}\ge4(1-1/20)=19/5.
\]
Since \(|A|\le1+3\mathbf1\{|A|\ge2\}\),
\[
 P_0\{|K(W)|\ge2\}\ge\frac{19/5-1}{3}=\frac{14}{15}.
\]
Uniquely labelled means approach the contact, and convolution with a Gaussian density makes bounded loss expectations continuous in the mean; hence \(R_0(K)\ge14/15\). The rule \(K_{\mathrm{ct}}\) includes each label with probability \(14/15+1/60=19/20\) and incurs loss only when it reports \(V_4\), with probability \(14/15\). It attains the bound.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: For every \(\mathfrak G\in\mathfrak E\), the value \(M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\) is attained by a globally honest randomized rule and equals the supremum of the Lagrange dual over finite nonnegative atomic coverage measures on the regions \(D_v\) and finite atomic probability measures on \(H_r\). Every finite atomic dual is a valid lower certificate. An increasing enumeration of finite atomic certificates with rational weights and rationally encoded real-algebraic support points converges upward to \(M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\), without a bounded-support premise.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The frozen phrase ‘rational atoms’ is stronger than the declared geometry guarantees if it means rational-coordinate support: a zero-dimensional rational semialgebraic component can have only algebraic points. The proved and algorithmically sufficient formulation uses rational weights and rational isolating encodings of real-algebraic support points; it leaves the finite-atomic dual equality and absence of a support bound unchanged.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Suppose \(c_n\to0\) and \(\max_{j\in\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}}\sup_{u\in C}|e_{n,j}(u)|\to0\) for every compact \(C\subset\mathbb R^d\). Every finite atomic dual certificate for \(\mathfrak G_0\), whose coverage and risk atoms lie in a compact local-direction set, transfers through the positive-cell multinomial comparison with a vanishing explicit remainder. Consequently \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}M_n\ge M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)\). No reverse \(\limsup\) inequality is asserted without a separately proved global transferred-primal construction.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current assumptions permit \(p_n(0)=p_0+n^{-1/4}z\) for a simplex-tangent \(z\), so an active slack has \(c_{n,j}=n^{1/4}\alpha_j^{\prime}z\) and the zero-offset experiment need not be the local limit. The reverse \(\limsup\) also requires a single globally honest transferred primal on the expanding lawful domain, which the compact comparison does not provide. The proposed claim retains the valid certificate-first lower converse, adds the necessary zero-offset condition, and does not assume the missing upper construction.

proposed_assumptions.condition: \(\mathcal F(p_0)\ne\varnothing\); equivalently, there exists \(P_0\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\) whose observed multinomial law satisfies \(p(P_0)=p_0\).
proposed_assumptions.reason: Multinomial interiority does not imply that the causal response-type fiber is nonempty. Without this condition the endpoint programs may have no feasible branch, so the claimed global tangent cover and strict semantic chamber do not follow.

proposed_assumptions.condition: The compact-uniform convergences of the moving-slack remainders are effective: from a rational compact polytope \(C\subset\mathbb R^d\) and a positive rational tolerance, an algorithm returns an index after which \(\max_{j\in\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}}\sup_{u\in C}|e_{n,j}(u)|\) is below that tolerance.
proposed_assumptions.reason: Qualitative compact-uniform convergence alone has no input-computable diagonal modulus. This effectiveness condition is needed only for the algorithmic schedule, not for the mathematical boundary comparison.

proposed.statement: Suppose \(c_n\to0\) and \(\max_{j\in\mathcal J_0^{\mathrm{act}}}\sup_{u\in C}|e_{n,j}(u)|\to0\) for every compact \(C\subset\mathbb R^d\). Every finite atomic dual certificate for \(\mathfrak G_0\), whose coverage and risk atoms lie in a compact local-direction set, transfers through the positive-cell multinomial comparison with a vanishing explicit remainder. Consequently \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}M_n\ge M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)\). No reverse \(\limsup\) inequality is asserted without a separately proved global transferred-primal construction.
proposed.justification: The order of limits gives a valid certificate-first lower converse once the local experiment is actually centered at the zero-offset fan.
proposed.gap: A two-sided minimax transfer additionally needs a single globally honest primal on the expanding lawful multinomial domain; compact comparison alone does not supply it.
proposed.consumer: The lower certificate justifies interpreting the Gaussian value as an asymptotic lower benchmark for the same declared Job Corps assertions under zero-offset centering.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The narrowed claim introduces the moving-slack quantities explicitly and removes dependencies used only by the unproved global upper transfer.
